risks.note: Base oil is the Company's principal input ('lubricating oils, greases, rubber process oils, and other derivatives derived from base oils'). The Directors' Report describes FY26 as 'a challenging business environment marked by fluctuations in crude oil and base oil prices, evolving global trade dynamics and intense market competition', and the MD&A states 'The unpredictable nature of prices of raw materials along with the changing consumer tastes towards advanced and high-end lubricants adds to the challenges that are faced regarding pricing and margins.' [BACK-FILLED: the MD&A 'RISKS & CHALLENGES' subsection is NOT in the risks_esg bundle - it was routed to the strategy_outlook and capex_expansion bundles; the Directors' Report quote is from the profile bundle.]
risks.risk: Crude oil and base oil price volatility driving raw-material cost and margin risk

risks.note: Present in this bundle's MD&A macro section ('The war situation prevailing in the Middle East region along with increasing prices of oil as well as other commodities has made global economic growth projections for 2026 uncertain') and stated as a direct business threat in the MD&A THREATS subsection: 'Any disturbances in the crude oil production, refining activities and shipping channels are likely to affect crude and base oil prices, freight costs and availability of crucial raw material inputs. High macroeconomic volatility could limit the demand for lubricants in both the automotive and industrial sectors.' [THREATS subsection BACK-FILLED from the strategy_outlook / capex_expansion bundles.]
risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict and supply-chain disruption in sourcing, freight and raw-material availability

risks.note: Management explicitly drew shareholders' attention to this as a watch item: 'Towards the end of the fourth quarter of FY 2025-26, geopolitical developments led to a sharp increase in crude-linked raw material costs and currency weakness, which may pose short-to-medium-term challenges for the industry.' Mitigation stated is disciplined cost control and pricing action. [BACK-FILLED from the Executive Director & CFO's message in the strategy_outlook and capex_expansion bundles - it is not in the risks_esg bundle.]
risks.risk: Near-term crude-linked input cost spike and currency weakness flagged at the end of Q4 FY2025-26

risks.note: The MD&A states 'Volatile forex movement also necessitates risk mitigation measures to ensure least impact on the profitability & margins.' The Company both imports inputs and exports to more than 12 countries, so the exposure is two-sided. No hedging policy, quantum or currency split is disclosed in any routed section. [BACK-FILLED from the MD&A 'RISKS & CHALLENGES' subsection in the strategy_outlook / capex_expansion bundles.]

Identified as the structural long-term threat: 'the trend of growing popularity of electric vehicles along with evolving environmental policies in several countries has changed lubricants' demand dynamics', and 'the gradual movement towards electric mobility could change the pattern of demand in the conventional lubricants category'. The Company frames it as partly offset by opportunities in EV-specific fluids, battery thermal management, coolants and specialty greases, and says it 'continues to stay vigilant of new trends'. No quantified exposure of revenue to ICE-linked products is given. [BACK-FILLED from the MD&A THREATS/OUTLOOK subsections in the strategy_outlook / capex_expansion bundles.]
risks.risk: Energy transition / electric mobility structurally altering conventional lubricant demand

risks.note: Stated in this bundle: IPOL is 'one of the few indigenous brands which were able to survive and sustain itself over the past five decades while being in competition with various multinational and even public-sector lubricants producers'; the MD&A adds 'In the Indian context, the environment is no different as organized players, multinationals and local manufacturers compete in variety of segments', and the Directors' Report cites 'intense market competition' as a feature of the FY26 environment.
risks.risk: Intense competition from multinationals, public-sector oil companies and local manufacturers

risks.note: 'The lubricant manufacturing industry is currently experiencing a major change due to technological developments and evolving customers' expectations along with stricter regulations... This has led to a shift for the industry away from volume-driven production to premium and application-oriented lubricant production.' Emissions, sustainable production, product quality and waste-management requirements 'necessitates regular investments into research and development, product development and quality assurance' - i.e. a standing cost of staying qualified. [BACK-FILLED from the MD&A 'RISKS & CHALLENGES' subsection.]
risks.risk: Technology and regulatory shift to premium, application-specific and low-emission products requiring continuous R&D investment

risks.note: The bitumen diversification rests on a small number of PSU counterparties (HPCL, BPCL, and IOCL via the JV). The AR states that on the first HPCL contract 'the off-take during the initial contract period was lower than the tendered quantity due to reduced demand from HPCL' - the tendered volume is therefore not a committed volume, and the renewal covers only the balance quantity. [BACK-FILLED from the MD&A Trading segment commentary in the strategy_outlook bundle. risks.risk: Customer/off-take concentration in the new bitumen vertical, evidenced by an off-take shortfall on the first PSU contract
